title: How to measure brand awareness: metrics, surveys and tracking
summary: Here is how to measure brand awareness beyond recall scores, with a survey and tracking framework that shows why your awareness score moved.
body_markdown:
How do we measure what people actually associate with our brand, not only whether they recognize the name? +


Measuring brand awareness beyond brand recognition means adding open-ended association questions answered in each participant's own words. Ask them to describe the brand and who it is for before any prompted list, so they cannot echo internal words like "trusted." Without that layer in the same study, the "why" behind brand perception never gets collected.


What should we add to an aided and unaided awareness tracker to explain why awareness is rising or falling? +


Add a qualitative layer to your brand awareness tracker, run with the same participants. Interviews explain which associations caused the change. Pair awareness with consideration measures, and treat unexpected movement as a trigger for focused follow-up before briefing any action to improve brand awareness.


How can we tell whether higher brand awareness reflects the positioning we intended or the wrong associations? +


Compare the brand identity the team intended to communicate with what participants say unprompted. Brand awareness can rise on the wrong associations while the tracker reports a win. Ask participants to describe the brand and its target audience in their own words, and what they remember from the last marketing campaign. Where answers diverge from the brief, positioning has drifted.


How often should we collect qualitative feedback alongside brand tracking so the findings arrive before campaign decisions are locked? +


Your brand awareness tracking cadence should include continuous or trigger-based qualitative feedback instead of waiting for the next scheduled wave. A study completed six months ago may no longer reflect the market. Add follow-ups whenever a score moves after specific marketing campaigns, so changes get explained while they still matter. That way, findings arrive while the decision is still open.


What should brand teams look for in a qualitative layer for brand tracking, if they need both awareness scores and the reasons behind them? +


Look for awareness scores and a qualitative layer tied to the same participants. On Conveo, teams pair unaided recall with each participant's own associations, so a rising score arrives with evidence of whether the brand resonates for the right reasons. In AI-moderated video interviews, each theme links to the participants behind it, with video clips and verbatim quotes stakeholders can audit. Use that standard to judge any qualitative layer added to a tracker.


What is the difference between measuring brand awareness and measuring brand associations? +


Brand awareness metrics confirm the brand exists in someone's memory, while associations capture what that name means to the person. Recall questions measure the first, and open-ended questions asked before any prompted list measure the second. Awareness can rise while associations drift, so track both as separate key metrics. Together they feed \[brand equity research\](/insights/brand-equity-research-methods-measure-brand-value), which links what people know about a brand to what it is worth.
